not_detected.summary: Turn on DKIM signing at your email provider and publish the key it gives you. We only test common selector names, so if DKIM is already on under a custom name, this result may be a false alarm.

microsoft365: In the Microsoft Defender portal, find the DKIM setting under email authentication settings and select your domain.
Microsoft shows two CNAME records (selector1 and selector2 under _domainkey). Publish both in your DNS manager.
Return to the DKIM page and switch signing on for the domain.
google: In the Google Admin console, open Gmail settings, then Authenticate email.
Select your domain and generate a new key, choosing a 2048-bit key.
Publish the TXT record it shows in your DNS manager, then click Start authentication.
cpanel: In cPanel open Email Deliverability and click Manage next to your domain.
If DKIM shows a problem, use the Repair or Install button. cPanel creates and publishes the key for you when it hosts your DNS.

generic: Generate a new 2048-bit key at your email provider and publish it under a new selector.
After mail is signing with the new key, remove the old selector's record.
Some DNS hosts limit TXT record length; a 2048-bit key may need to be split into two quoted strings in one record.

fail.summary: The key is too weak or unreadable. Generate a new 2048-bit key at your email provider and publish it.

generic: Generate a new 2048-bit key at your email provider.
Publish it, confirm signing works, then remove the broken record.
